rule: **C4 Unresolved references are preserved.** A call the tool cannot resolve is still emitted as a low guess (`recv.m`, `.m`, a bare name). It is never dropped and never promoted to a resolved ID. | Call on a receiver of **unknown type**: `recv.member`, using the LAST receiver segment (`self.client.get()` → `client.get`; `a.b.c()` → `b.c`). | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member`
notes: No namespace → class ID Legacy. $client and $payload have no declared type → recv.member with the last receiver segment; the `$` sigil is not part of the name (SPEC writes the PHP named nested function `$f = function` as `outer.f`). build() has no declared return type, so its result is a computed receiver → .commit; an index (`items[0]`) is a computed receiver → .flush. undefined_helper is a bare name not found in the scan (global namespace, so no fallback question) → low, direct. call_type: SPEC lists direct|method without defining them; this corpus uses method for every callee of the form Type#m / recv.m / .m (instance and static member calls) and direct for free functions, bare names and named nested functions.
